profile.campus: Legacy Stream asset (Richardson, TX, DFW IV) - sold 2011, no longer Stream-operated, unrelated to the later DFWA site in Garland
profile.reading: Stream DFW IV sits at 3300 Essex Drive in Richardson, Texas, a legacy Stream asset rather than a currently Stream-operated facility. Per Stream own site, the building provided 1.68 megawatts of capacity, expandable to 2.3 megawatts, across 20,000 square feet including a 10,000 square foot data hall. Stream leased the facility to an unnamed major healthcare provider in early 2011 and sold it later that same year to a real estate investment trust, whose identity could not be independently confirmed this session, though a 2011 SEC filing from Carter Validus Mission Critical REIT surfaced as a plausible but unverified match during this research and is not asserted here as confirmed. Because Stream sold the property in 2011, roughly nine years before its DFWA facility in nearby Garland was commissioned, DFW IV and DFWA should be understood as unrelated Stream projects in the same broad Dallas-Fort Worth market rather than phases of one campus, and this record should be read as documenting the facility Stream-era history rather than its current ownership or operator, which is unconfirmed. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership of Stream itself has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. Richardson sits in the northern Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, an established telecom and technology corridor sometimes referred to locally as the Telecom Corridor given its concentration of network and hardware companies dating back to the 1980s and 1990s, a heritage consistent with this building relatively small, early-2010s-era footprint compared to the much larger hyperscale-oriented facilities Stream has built more recently elsewhere in the same metro area.
profile.research_note: 1.68MW expandable to 2.3MW / 20,000 sqft (10,000 sqft data hall) sourced to Stream own DFW IV page. 2011 lease-then-sale to a REIT confirmed via Stream own site, exact REIT buyer unconfirmed, a Carter Validus Mission Critical REIT 2011 10-Q surfaced as plausible but explicitly flagged as unverified rather than stated as fact.
sources_tried: Streams own Dallas locations page, Streams own Apollo acquisition press release, and Apollos own completion press release

reading.body:
Stream DFW IV in Richardson is one of four Stream Data Centers campuses in the Dallas-Fort Worth region that the operator lists on its own site, and the only one with a tracked address in this registry. The facility's power capacity is not published. Without a published figure, this campus cannot be ranked among Texas's 18 facilities with disclosed capacity, though it sits in a region where Stream operates multiple sites whose aggregate scale is material to the operator's portfolio.

Stream was acquired by Apollo Global Management in November 2025, with Apollo taking a majority stake and the management team retaining a minority position. The company reports more than 90 percent of capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers across a portfolio described as 20 to 27 delivered campuses and a 4 plus gigawatt development pipeline. Stream's published materials do not disclose individual campus power ratings or the capacity contribution of DFW IV to the company's Texas footprint.

Texas hosts 133 mapped data center facilities and publishes capacity figures for 18 of them, totaling 468.41 megawatts. DFW IV's unpublished power rating means this campus cannot be assessed against that state total or the rank of published sites. The facility's relevance to AI scaling capacity in Texas cannot be determined from public specification.
